summary: Add one to a number represented as a list of digits (most significant first).
mainInsight: Add the 1 as an initial carry at the least significant digit and propagate it leftwards while digits overflow from 9 to 0; only if the carry survives past the front do you need a new leading 1.

approaches.name: Convert to int
weaknesses: Defeats the point; breaks in fixed-width languages

approaches.name: Right-to-left carry
approaches.summary: Add the carry from the end; digit becomes total % 10, carry total // 10; prepend 1 if carry remains.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal. Mutates the input list (usually fine).

promptVariants: How should the +1 be propagated across the digit array?
options: Right-to-left pass, carrying the overflow along
Left-to-right pass with a stack for the digits
Binary search for the digit position to increment
Sorting the digits and adding one to the largest
cards.answer: Right-to-left pass, carrying the overflow along
cards.explanation: Addition proceeds from the least significant digit, which is at the end of the array.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Left-to-right pass with a stack for the: Unnecessary; the carry flows right to left.

promptVariants: When can the loop stop early, and what is the only case that grows the array?
Which input forces a new leading digit?
cards.answer: As soon as a digit becomes <= 8 after adding the carry there is no further carry, so the rest stays untouched. The array only grows when every digit was 9 (e.g. 999 -> 1000), leaving a carry after the first digit.
cards.explanation: Most inputs finish in O(1) steps in practice.

promptVariants: Which input needs a new most significant digit?
cards.explanation: Every 9 becomes 0 with a carry, and the final carry becomes a new leading 1.

promptVariants: Plus One touches each digit at most once, so it is ___ time.
cards.explanation: At most one pass over the digits (all 9s).

promptVariants: What is the space complexity, and when is it not O(1)?
Is Plus One really O(1) space? When does it allocate?
cards.answer: O(1) extra since digits are updated in place; in the all-9s case you allocate a new list of length n+1, which is O(n).
cards.explanation: Mutating the input may or may not be acceptable.

promptVariants: Why initialise carry = 1 and loop `while i >= 0 and carry`?
How does starting with carry = 1 replace special-casing the +1?
cards.code:
i = len(digits) - 1
carry = 1
while i >= 0 and carry:
    total = digits[i] + carry
    digits[i] = total % 10
    carry = total // 10
    i -= 1
if carry:
    return [1] + digits
return digits
cards.answer: Treating the +1 as an initial carry makes the first step identical to every later step, so no special case is needed. The loop ends when the carry disappears or the digits run out; a leftover carry means all digits were 9.
